title: Rav Kahana (V), Rav Ashi’s Colleague
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He was Rav Papa’s student, as in Shabbat 89a: a certain scholar said to Rav Kahana, “Why are you not found before Rav Papa and Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua, who study aggadah?” Hyman suggests that apparently he listened to that scholar’s advice, as we find in Ketubot 86a: Rav Kahana said to Rav Papa: “According to you, who said that repaying a creditor is a mitzvah — if he says, ‘I do not wish to perform a mitzvah,’ what?” He said to him: “We learned,” etc. In Gittin 89b he raised a difficulty against Rav Papa, who said to him: “It is different there.”

He likewise sat before Rav Pappi and Rav Zevid, as in Sotah 45a: Rav Kahana said to Rav Pappi — and some say to Rav Zevid — “Let the Master resolve it from Rabbi Abbahu.” He said to him: “And according to your reasoning,” etc. In Bava Metzia 101a: Rav Kahana said to Rav Pappi — and some say to Rav Zevid — “But that which was taught,” etc. In Bava Batra 132b: Rav Pappi thought to say … Rav Kahana said to him, “If,” etc. In Me’ilah 19a: Rav Kahana said to Rav Zevid, “And gold not?” He said to him, “Perhaps.” Hyman distinguishes him from Rav Zevid of Nehardea and identifies him as the Rav Zevid who headed the academy in Pumbedita and died in the year 696 of the Seleucid era (lishtarot).

He likewise sat before Rav Shimi bar Ashi, as in Chullin 11b: “Rav Kahana said: I said the teaching before Rav Shimi [bar Ashi],” and so it is in Temurah 28a; in Zevachim 71b Hyman considers “Rav Ashi said” erroneous and proposes Rav Kahana; and in Chullin 53a, Rav Kahana in the name of Rav Shimi bar Ashi. According to the testimony of Rav Sherira Gaon in his Epistle, part 3, end of chapter 3, Rav Kahana headed the academy in Pumbedita after Rafram from the year 706 to 725. In Hyman’s account, although he was head of the academy there, Rav Ashi’s academy in Sura was the great academy, and all were subordinate to it, because there they arranged the Talmud, and all the sages of the generation would gather there periodically to establish teachings according to the halakhah. Therefore we find in Berakhot 24a: Rav Kahana said to Rav Ashi, “There Rava said … here, what?” He said to him: “Did he cast them all into one mold?” In Menachot 106a: Rav Kahana said to Rav Ashi, “But there is room for doubt … for Rava said.” In Ketubot 20b: Rav Ashi knew testimony for Rav Kahana. Rav Kahana said to Rav Ashi, “Does the Master remember this testimony?” Rav Ashi said, “No.” In the end Rav Ashi remembered and testified for him. He saw that Rav Kahana was hesitating, and said to him: “Do you think I am relying on you?” etc.

The book Dor Dor veDorshav, part 3, end of chapter 16, p. 182, says that this Rav Kahana who headed the academy in Pumbedita is Rav Ashi’s teacher; Hyman respectfully rejects that identification. Hyman states that this Rav Kahana died thirteen years before Rav Ashi, but Rav Kahana, Rav Ashi’s teacher, died many years before this Rav Kahana. Hyman regards this as clear.

notes.text: Saved Davidson Ketubot20b has KAHANA asking ASHI whether he remembers, ASHI saying no and later recalling; the draft reversed the initial speakers. Hyman’s Zevid and Kahana distinctions and Sura-wide subordination claim remain attributed.696Seleucid and706–725 are retained without new conversion. The stated thirteen-year interval is retained.

The consulted Ketubot 20b recounts Rav Ashi recalling testimony for Rav Kahana; Kahana asks whether Ashi remembers, and Ashi later says that he recalled it himself. This does not independently establish Hyman’s separation of the Kahanas, his identification of Zevid, the thirteen-year interval, or the reconstruction of Sura’s supremacy and the arrangement of the Talmud. His exact Epistle, Dor Dor veDorshav and textual-emendation claims remain attributed; 696 Seleucid and the supplied 706–725 remain without new conversion. His conclusion retains its clear force.
